chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Qattan told us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Sukkari told us, saying: Abu Abdillah al-Ghulabi told us, saying: Mahduj ibn Umayr al-Hanafi told us, saying: Bishr ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari narrated from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from his father, from Abu Huraira, who said:
Fatima was only named Fatima because Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, separated those who love her from the Fire.
ai.seo_question: Why is Fatima called Fatima and what is the meaning of her name in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* links the name Fatima to the root 'fatama' (to wean/separate), asserting that Allah separates her lovers from the Hellfire. While often cited in Shia tradition to support the concept of *shafa'ah* (intercession) and the spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt, it is important to note that this specific narration is classified as *mashhur* (well-known) and is primarily found in Sunni sources like al-Tabarani, rather than being exclusive to Shia hadith collections. The statement emphasizes a divine act of protection for her devotees, reinforcing the theological significance of love for Fatima (SA) in Shia piety.
